text:
During an employment tribunal, you may have to:

provide documents or other evidence

answer questions about what happened

attend a hearing

explain how you calculated any compensation you’re asking for

A tribunal cannot guarantee that you will win your case or receive compensation.

If you have a health condition that could affect you taking part in a hearing, you can tell the tribunal at any time during the process that you may need reasonable adjustments.

What a tribunal costs

You do not have to pay a fee to make a claim to an employment tribunal.

You may have to pay other costs, such as:

witness expenses

legal fees

the respondent’s costs, if the tribunal decides you’ve acted unreasonably

You can find guidance about what it might cost to make a claim to an employment tribunal on Citizens Advice.

What you could get from a tribunal

If you win your case at the employment tribunal, they may order the respondent to pay you compensation. A tribunal does not usually order an employer to apologise.

If you lose your case at the employment tribunal, you can appeal or ask the tribunal to reconsider the decision.

How long a tribunal takes

There is no fixed length of time for an employment tribunal claim. How long it takes depends on:

the type and complexity of the case

how many hearings are needed

After your final hearing, you’ll receive the decision within a few weeks.
